Definition: of Hebrew origin (H3327); Isaac (i.e. Jitschak), the son of Abraham:--Isaac.
BiblicalUsage: Isaac is the son of the promise, the child Abraham waited for, and the New Testament holds him up as the pattern of faith. In Matthew 1:2 Abraham begat Isaac, and Isaac begat Jacob, in Hebrews 11:17 Abraham offered up Isaac when he was tried, and in Galatians 4:28 Paul says, we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Isaac is the proof that God's promises are born, not earned: the child of old age became the father of the nation, and we are his children by promise too.
RelatedEvents: The Binding of Isaac; The Birth of Jesus
